positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: ETH remains the clearest active-catalyst leader on the tape. US spot Ether ETFs are on a sustained inflow streak — $60.86M (Aug 5) and $92.15M (Aug 6), pushing the weekly total to ~$244.94M, a 4-month high — led by BlackRock's ETHA. ETH/BTC is still testing a nine-year breakout level, backed by whale accumulation. Canonical dashboard proxy was FRESH this run (asOf 2026-08-08T11:52:51Z): ETH 1918.99, BTC 64928.31, SOL 75.41, pulled at run time ~2026-08-08T11:55Z.
positions.driver: Closed prior ETH at 1918.99 (canonical live) vs entry 1913.32 for +31.66 (+0.30%) — ETH firmed further overnight, holding above the $1,900 pivot while BTC stayed flat (~64.9k). RE-SELECTED ETH as the best risk-adjusted next-24h pick: it owns the strongest active flow catalyst (multi-session record ETP inflows + nine-year ETH/BTC breakout in progress) and the cleanest relative strength. Wins vs runners-up: BTC (~64.9k) is the safe major but drifting — its ETF inflows still are not translating into price, so no near-term edge; SOL bounced to 75.41 (from 73.54) but remains below its ~$77 pivot with higher beta and higher stop-out odds. ETH offers the asymmetric setup with a definable 8% major stop.
positions.risks: ETH has run into the ETF-flow narrative and consolidates in a tight $1,910-$1,918 range — flow-driven moves can cool off quickly and Friday's US jobs print is the key macro swing factor; a risk-off surprise could trigger sharp mean-reversion. ETH/BTC nine-year breakouts can fail and retrace. Hard stop 1765.47 (-8%).
